stimulus.text: Alexander Hamilton, Report on Public Credit, January 1790: “A national debt, if it is not excessive, will be to us a national blessing.” Paraphrase: Hamilton proposed that the federal government pay the national debt at full value and take over the states’ war debts, funding both by selling government bonds.
stimulus.source_note: Alexander Hamilton, Report on Public Credit, January 1790. Public domain.

source: original; stimulus quotes Hamilton, Report on Public Credit, January 1790, public domain.

primary_sources: Alexander Hamilton, Report on Public Credit (January 1790)

stem: Why did Hamilton want the federal government to take over the states’ war debts?

options.text: To punish the states that had borrowed the most during the war.
options.misconception: Hamilton wanted to bind the states to the Union, not to punish them.

options.text: To let each state print its own paper money again.
options.misconception: The plan was about debts, not about state paper money.

options.text: To keep the national debt small by spreading it among the states.
options.misconception: Assumption made the national debt larger, not smaller.

options.text: To tie wealthy creditors and the states to the national government.

rationales.D: Background: creditors owed money by the national government would want that government to survive and prosper.
rationales.A: Hamilton’s aim was to bind creditors to the Union, not to punish any state.
rationales.B: Background: Hamilton worked toward a single national money system, not state paper money.
rationales.C: Taking over state debts made the national debt larger, not smaller.
rationales.general:
1. The stimulus says Hamilton would take over the states’ war debts and fund them with bonds.
2. Background: the people holding those bonds would then be paid by the national government, not by their states.
3. A creditor paid by the national government has a reason to want that government to last.
4. So assumption was political as well as financial: it tied rich and powerful people to the Union.
Remember: follow the money to find the loyalty; whoever pays a debt gains a supporter.
